title: Mata Sahib Kaur, mother of the Khalsa
hookLine: at amrit, Sikhs are told Mata Sahib Kaur is their spiritual mother

cards: Who are your parents? Most days that's a simple question. But at a Sikh amrit ceremony, once the new initiates have taken the amrit, they are given a second family on top of the one they were born into.
They are told who their spiritual father is, who their spiritual mother is, and where their spiritual home is. People come to that moment from every kind of family. Some have lost a mother.
Some never knew one. Some have a wonderful one. And all of them, standing together, are handed the same name.

teach.h: A WIFE OF GURU GOBIND SINGH.
teach.b: Mata Sahib Kaur was a wife of Guru Gobind Singh.
Tradition says she had no children of her own, and that the Guru told her she would be the mother of a much larger family: the Khalsa. That is how Sikhs remember her.

teach.h: YOUR MOTHER IS MATA SAHIB KAUR.
teach.b: At amrit, the new members of the Khalsa are told: your father is Guru Gobind Singh, your mother is Mata Sahib Kaur, and your home is Anandpur.
A shopkeeper's son and a farmer's daughter, people whose families might never have shared a meal, walk out of the ceremony as brothers and sisters, with the same mother.

teach.h: A FAMILY MADE BY THE BOWL.
teach.b: The family is not made by blood. It's made by the bowl. Two days ago, with Mata Jito, we heard that some tellings say it was Mata Sahib Kaur who added the sweets to the first amrit.
Either way, the tellings put a woman's hand in that first bowl. After the Guru's death she lived in Delhi beside Mata Sundari, and tradition says she, too, sent letters of guidance to the sangats.
Here is the quiet surprise in her story.

A woman with no children of her own is remembered as mother to every member of the Khalsa. Being a mother, in this telling, is not only about giving birth. It's about who you hold, who you claim, who you treat as yours.
And every time a new Sikh takes amrit, her name is said again.

how: At an amrit ceremony, the new initiates are told that their spiritual father is Guru Gobind Singh, their spiritual mother is Mata Sahib Kaur, and their home is Anandpur Sahib.

practice: Think of a woman who cared for you in a way she didn't have to: a grandmother, an aunt, a teacher, a friend's mom whose kitchen was always open. Remember one specific thing she did.
If she's gone, say her name quietly, and say thank you.
